Daily Page rough · 2026-10-22 · Typography as Meaning

The conversation ladder

One balloon is a word with a face. Two balloons are a conversation, and then every balloon has to know where the others are. These frames climb slowly: two or three bits of text each, one rule per frame. Each one shows the fix beside the mistake, and a checker looks at the panel and says what's wrong with it: tails that cross, a tail running through another balloon, a face covered, a balloon in the line of sight between the two people, a reading order that runs backwards in time.

What the research says
  • Time runs down the panel. Read top to bottom; balloons at the same height read left to right (Kurlander et al., Comic Chat, SIGGRAPH 1996). Never place a reply above the line it answers, and don't set two balloons at the same height, which is a coin flip (Merritt Houghton).
  • The first speaker should stand on the left; when the art won't allow it, flop the panel (Todd Klein).
  • Tails never cross. If they must, the balloons are in the wrong place (Klein; Waterman). Comic Chat places every balloon body first while reserving a lane for each tail, and draws the tails last.
  • Tails aim at the mouth and stop about halfway to it; short tails are intimate, long ones mean distance or shouting (Blambot, Waterman).
  • One speaker's balloons in a row join along one arc to the mouth, and the join widens away from the speaker; a second balloon is a beat, a pause (Balloon Tales, Merritt Houghton).
  • Butted or overlapping balloons are an interruption; the cut-off line ends in a double dash (Waterman, Blambot).
  • Keep balloons out of the line of sight between two people, and off their faces (Balloon Tales, Klein).
  • A thought trail points at the head, not the mouth (Blambot). An off-panel voice runs its tail to the frame's edge.

Built from Typography as Meaning's grammar, with fonts from BLUELINE's lettering bench. The balloon positions in these frames are placed by hand; the tails, joins, trails and every check are computed. The next rung is a solver that places the balloons itself, Comic Chat's way, and passes these same checks.
